entities.summary:
Shalmaneser IV was the king of the Neo-Assyrian Empire from 783 BC to 771 BC, ruling during a period of decline from which few sources survive. He was the son and successor of his predecessor, Adad-nirari III, and his reign was marked by an increase in the power held by Assyrian officials relative to that of the king. Assyria's enemies, including the Medes and Babylonians, grew increasingly powerful during his time in office.

Shalmaneser IV's reign was also notable for the construction of several temples and monuments, including the temple at Ashur, which was dedicated to the god Ashur. The extent of his military campaigns is not well documented, but it is known that he fought against the Medes and Babylonians, and that he was eventually succeeded by his son, Ashur-etil-ilani.

Despite the scarcity of information about his reign, Shalmaneser IV remains an important figure in the history of the Neo-Assyrian Empire, and his legacy continues to be studied by historians and scholars today.

As the last great king of the Neo-Assyrian Empire, Shalmaneser IV's reign marked the beginning of the end of Assyrian power and influence, paving the way for the rise of the Babylonians and the eventual fall of the empire.

The fall of the Neo-Assyrian Empire had a profound impact on the ancient world, leading to the spread of Babylonian culture and the eventual rise of new powers such as the Persians.

In conclusion, Shalmaneser IV's reign may have been marked by decline and instability, but it was also a time of significant cultural and military achievement, and his legacy continues to be felt in the ancient world today.


Shalmaneser IV was a skilled diplomat and strategist who successfully navigated the complex web of alliances and rivalries that characterized the ancient Near East during his reign.

The Neo-Assyrian Empire, under Shalmaneser IV, was a major power in the ancient Near East, with a vast network of trade routes and a powerful military.
